name: The Brando
positioning: Private-villa resort on Tetiaroa, the coral atoll Marlon Brando fell for, a 20-minute flight from Tahiti
best_for: Couples who want a private villa with its own plunge pool on a remote atoll
Nature lovers keen on guided reef, bird and turtle excursions
Travelers who care about sustainability and Polynesian culture

facts.text: The resort sits on Tetiaroa, an atoll encircled by a coral reef with 12 motus, or islets.
Guests fly into Faa'a International Airport in Papeete, Tahiti, then take Air Tetiaroa on a 20-minute scenic flight to the atoll.
Marlon Brando first spied Tetiaroa on a hike in Tahiti while filming Mutiny on the Bounty in the early 1960s.
The resort opened in 2014, after the Brando Family Trust approved Pacific Beachcomber's plan for it in 2009.
The private villas are spread across the Onetahi motu, set back just off the beach, alongside one private residence.
Villa doors fold open to create breezeways to the outdoors.
The One Bedroom Villa has an outdoor lounge area on the deck, an outdoor covered dining area and an infinity plunge pool.
On the atoll, buildings are cooled with seawater, solar panels light the paths at night, and glass is returned to sand.
Varua Te Ora Polynesian Spa is reached by elevated pathways that wind through tropical undergrowth to secluded spaces for relaxation and healing.
Fare Mana, just off the sand, hosts meditation, yoga and sound baths.
Green sea turtles nest on Tetiaroa from September to March.
The resort's cooking is a fusion of Polynesian flavors and classical French techniques.

highlights.text: During nesting season, guests can join Te Mana o Te Moana marine biologists on night patrols looking for nesting turtles or emerging hatchlings.
The Brando was the first resort globally to receive LEED Platinum Certification.
Fare Manu, 'the bird house', is a treetop treatment space for two within the spa.
Reef Quest is a snorkeling trip to coral gardens on the outer barrier reef, for confident swimmers aged 12 and up.
Bob's Bar is Marlon Brando's original beachside bar, serving the signature 'Bob's Last Drop' cocktail.

considerations.text: Getting there takes a second flight: after landing in Papeete, Tahiti, guests take Air Tetiaroa on a 20-minute flight to the atoll.
Turtle nesting runs from September to March, so the night patrols are seasonal.
WhataHotel notes ultra-premium pricing that reflects the resort's exclusivity.
